question: If cosec A = (5)/(4) , then the value of sin 2A + 2cos 2A is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

cosec A = 5/4 ⇒ sin A = 4/5 ⇒ cos A = 3/5

Use identities: sin2A = 2sinAcosA, cos2A = cos²A − sin²A

sin2A = 2×4/5×3/5 = 24/25

cos2A = 9/25 − 16/25 = −7/25

**∴ Answer = 2/25**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

cosec A = 5/4

**Formula used:**

sin A = 1/cosec A, sin2A = 2sinAcosA, cos2A = cos²A − sin²A

**Calculation:**

⇒ sin A = 4/5

⇒ cos A = √(1 − sin²A)

⇒ = √(1 − 16/25) = √(9/25) = 3/5

⇒ sin2A = 2 × 4/5 × 3/5 = 24/25

⇒ cos2A = (3/5)² − (4/5)²

⇒ = 9/25 − 16/25 = −7/25

⇒ sin2A + 2cos2A = 24/25 + 2(−7/25)

⇒ = 24/25 − 14/25

⇒ = 10/25 = 2/5

**∴ The correct answer is 2/5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Reciprocal Identities

cosec A = 1/sin A

Double Angle Formula

sin2A = 2sinAcosA, cos2A = cos²A − sin²A

Pythagorean Identity

sin²A + cos²A = 1

Shortcut Tip

Use right triangle values for quick calculation
